name: The museum's own travertine offcuts crushed to a 0/6 sand and bound as a stabilised walk

diffuseAlbedo.derivation: the stone's own colour: crushing shows fresh fractures of the same calcite, and the binder keeps the sand's colour (Workings/rolled.stabilised.json: look)
diffuseAlbedo.note: A crushed face of a light stone reads a little paler than its sawn face; no measured colour of crushed travertine was read.

refractiveIndex.source: Shading/Substances/travertine.json: dielectric.refractiveIndex (calcite, from the record's F0)
refractiveIndex.derivation: the grains are the stone's calcite

porosity.source: Workings/rolled.stabilised.json: process ('sets into a weak, still-porous crust') and Shading/Substances/crushed-limestone.json (0.35 for loose angular stones)
porosity.note: No void ratio of a stabilised walk was read: a first value a little below the loose aggregate's, the binder filling some of the voids.

wettingDepth.source: Shading/Substances/crushed-limestone.json (the soils' and aggregates' first wetting depth)
wettingDepth.note: The depth whose pores govern the face's look when wet: the stabilised crust darkens when it rains.

grain.note: The finest structure the face shows from a walk: the finer grains of the grading, the dust between them unresolved.

bed.source: Workings/rolled.stabilised.json: the 0/6,3 grading (Bronzo Perasso: 'Sable naturel pour sols stabilises 0/6,3')
bed.note: The coarsest structure the face shows: its largest grain.

bedAspect.derivation: unbedded: crushing destroys the stone's bands

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the crushed limestone's.

toneSpread.note: The grains carry the stone's own variation of tone.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
